checks.corrected_quote: As these technologies continue to evolve, Congress must ensure we have transparent and reliable data to better understand how AI is impacting workers, industries, and local economies — including communities like Guam.
checks.note: Quote is attributed to Rep. James Moylan and appears verbatim; the item truncates the sentence before ' — including communities like Guam.' Moylan is a co-lead of the AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act, a data/reporting bill, consistent with the 'targeted transparency rule' claim.

Article (Jul 28, 2025) covers Moylan's office review of H.R.1 effects on Guam (Social Security, tipped income, SNAP, Medicaid/Medicare). Fetched text contains no mention of AI, artificial intelligence, or a moratorium, so the negative claim (no position taken) is accurate. Note this is absence-of-evidence, not evidence of a preemption stance; null score is appropriate.

The release's list of measures advanced at the Jan 21, 2026 markup includes 'H.R. 6275 - China AI Power Report Act'. The page does not name Moylan; sponsorship is established by the UHRP page (item 4). Release text still has an unfilled 'XX measures' placeholder.

Page names Rep. James Moylan (R-GU) as introducer on Nov 21, 2025 with co-sponsors Vindman and Huizenga. Quote appears verbatim. Page lists Chinese AI chips/semiconductors, military AI models, and AI used to surveil Uyghurs as report topics, matching the claim. Bill is a Commerce reporting requirement, not itself an export control.

score_objections.objection: The only evidence is the China AI Power Report Act, which requires Commerce to report annually on Chinese AI capabilities (chips, military models, surveillance). It is a monitoring/transparency bill and does not itself tighten export controls or state a position on chip sales. That supports a hawkish lean, but -2 'Tighten export controls' overstates what these sources show.

No source here addresses Big Tech regulation directly. The only related evidence is co-leading a workforce-data reporting bill about AI layoffs, which is a narrow transparency requirement on employers/agencies. It is compatible with -1 'Targeted rules' but the evidence is thin; if this is the sole basis, consider whether the dimension should be scored at all.
